column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|11-29|1780|Μαρία Θηρεσία|Maria Theresa|Maria Theresa was archduchess of Austria and queen of Hungary and Bohemia from 1740. She was the only woman to rule the Habsburg lands and carried out reforms in administration and education. She died in 1780.

bio|11-29|1803|Κρίστιαν Ντόπλερ|Christian Doppler|Christian Doppler was an Austrian physicist. He formulated the Doppler effect, the change in the frequency of waves when the source moves in relation to the observer. He died in 1853.
bio|11-29|1832|Λουίζα Μέι Όλκοτ|Louisa May Alcott|Louisa May Alcott was an American writer. She wrote the novel "Little Women" in 1868, drawing on material from her own family. She died in 1888.
bio|11-29|1898|Κλάιβ Στέιπλς Λιούις|C. S. Lewis|C. S. Lewis was born in 1898 in Belfast. He was a British writer and professor and wrote "The Chronicles of Narnia". He died in 1963.

bio|11-29|1924|Τζάκομο Πουτσίνι|Giacomo Puccini|Giacomo Puccini was an Italian composer. He wrote the operas "La Bohème", "Tosca", "Madama Butterfly" and "Turandot", which was left unfinished. He died in 1924.
bio|11-29|1932|Ζακ Σιράκ|Jacques Chirac|Jacques Chirac was a French politician. He was mayor of Paris, prime minister and president of France from 1995 to 2007. He died in 2019.

bio|11-29|1973|Ράιαν Γκιγκς|Ryan Giggs|Ryan Giggs is a former Welsh footballer. He played his entire career for Manchester United, winning 13 English league titles and two Champions Leagues. He also became a coach of the Wales national team.
bio|11-29|1986|Κάρι Γκραντ|Cary Grant|Cary Grant was a British actor who lived in Hollywood. He appeared in the films "North by Northwest" and "To Catch a Thief". He died in 1986.
bio|11-30|1667|Τζόναθαν Σουίφτ|Jonathan Swift|Jonathan Swift was an Irish writer and clergyman. He wrote "Gulliver's Travels" in 1726 and "A Modest Proposal". He died in 1745.
bio|11-30|1718|Κάρολος ΙΒ΄|Charles XII|Charles XII was king of Sweden from 1697. He fought the Great Northern War against Russia and was killed in 1718 at the siege of Fredriksten, in Norway.

bio|11-30|1817|Τέοντορ Μόμσεν|Theodor Mommsen|Theodor Mommsen was a German historian and jurist. He wrote "The History of Rome" and in 1902 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1903.

bio|11-30|1835|Μαρκ Τουέιν|Mark Twain|Mark Twain, whose real name was Samuel Clemens, was an American writer. He wrote "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" and "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn". He died in 1910.

bio|11-30|1874|Ουίνστον Τσόρτσιλ|Winston Churchill|Winston Churchill was a British politician. He was prime minister of the United Kingdom during the Second World War and led the resistance to Nazi Germany. In 1953 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1965.
bio|11-30|1900|Όσκαρ Ουάιλντ|Oscar Wilde|Oscar Wilde died in 1900 in Paris. He was an Irish writer, with works such as "The Picture of Dorian Gray" and "The Importance of Being Earnest".

bio|11-30|1935|Φερνάντο Πεσσόα|Fernando Pessoa|Fernando Pessoa was a Portuguese poet. He wrote under many heteronyms, and his work "The Book of Disquiet" became known after his death. He died in 1935, in Lisbon.
bio|11-30|1982|Ελίσα Κάθμπερτ|Elisha Cuthbert|Elisha Cuthbert is a Canadian actress. She became known with the series "24" and with the film "The World of Hell".
bio|11-30|1990|Μάγκνους Κάρλσεν|Magnus Carlsen|Magnus Carlsen is a Norwegian chess player. He became a grandmaster at the age of 13 and was world champion from 2013 to 2023.

bio|11-30|2013|Πολ Γουόκερ|Paul Walker|Paul Walker was killed on 30 November 2013 in a car accident in California, at the age of 40. He was an American actor, known from the "Fast and Furious" film series.

bio|12-01|1135|Ερρίκος Α΄|Henry I|Henry I was king of England from 1100 to 1135. He was the son of William the Conqueror and strengthened the administration of the kingdom. He died in 1135 in Normandy.
bio|12-01|1825|Αλέξανδρος Α΄|Alexander I|Alexander I was tsar of Russia from 1801. He defeated Napoleon in 1812 and was one of the leaders of the Holy Alliance. He died in 1825 at Taganrog.
bio|12-01|1896|Γκεόργκι Ζούκοφ|Georgy Zhukov|Georgy Zhukov was a Soviet marshal. He led the Red Army in decisive battles of the Second World War, such as those of Moscow and Berlin. He died in 1974.
bio|12-01|1935|Γούντι Άλεν|Woody Allen|Woody Allen is an American director, screenwriter and actor. He has directed films such as "Annie Hall" and "Manhattan" and has won Oscars.
bio|12-01|1945|Μπέτι Μίντλερ|Bette Midler|Bette Midler is an American singer and actress. She became known with the hits "The Rose" and "Wind Beneath My Wings".

bio|12-01|1947|Γκόντφρεϊ Χάρολντ Χάρντι|Godfrey Harold Hardy|Godfrey Harold Hardy was an English mathematician. He contributed to number theory and wrote "A Mathematician's Apology". He discovered the talent of the Indian mathematician Srinivasa Ramanujan. He died in 1947.

bio|12-01|1949|Πάμπλο Εσκομπάρ|Pablo Escobar|Pablo Escobar was a Colombian drug trafficker and the head of the Medellín cartel. He was responsible for many murders and bomb attacks. He was killed in 1993.

bio|12-01|1949|Σεμπαστιάν Πινιέρα|Sebastián Piñera|Sebastián Piñera was a Chilean businessman and politician. He was president of Chile from 2010 to 2014 and from 2018 to 2022. He died in 2024 in a plane crash.
bio|12-01|1973|Νταβίντ Μπεν Γκουριόν|David Ben-Gurion|David Ben-Gurion died in 1973. He was the first prime minister of Israel and a leader in the founding of the state in 1948.
bio|12-02|1547|Ερνάν Κορτές|Hernán Cortés|Hernán Cortés was a Spanish conquistador. He conquered the Aztec Empire in Mexico in 1521, with the help of local allies. He died in 1547.

bio|12-02|1594|Γεράρδος Μερκάτορ|Gerardus Mercator|Gerardus Mercator was a Flemish cartographer. In 1569 he created the Mercator projection, which preserves angles and helped sailors, and he introduced the term "atlas" for a collection of maps. He died in 1594.

bio|12-02|1814|Μαρκήσιος ντε Σαντ|Marquis de Sade|The Marquis de Sade was a French writer and politician. His works, such as "The 120 Days of Sodom", had harsh and crude content, and he himself spent years in prison. He died in 1814.

bio|12-02|1825|Πέτρος Β΄|Pedro II|Pedro II was emperor of Brazil from 1831 to 1889, when he was deposed and the republic was founded. During his reign slavery was abolished, in 1888. He died in 1891 in Paris.

bio|12-02|1859|Ζωρζ Σερά|Georges Seurat|Georges Seurat was a French painter. He was the founder of pointillism, with small dots of colour, and he painted "A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte". He died young, in 1891, at the age of 31.
bio|12-02|1978|Νέλι Φουρτάντο|Nelly Furtado|Nelly Furtado is a Canadian singer of Portuguese origin. She became known with hits such as "I'm Like a Bird" and "Promiscuous".

bio|12-02|1981|Μπρίτνεϊ Σπίαρς|Britney Spears|Britney Spears is an American singer. She became known in 1998 with the hit "...Baby One More Time" and is regarded as one of the biggest names in pop music of the 2000s.
bio|12-02|1993|Πάμπλο Εσκομπάρ|Pablo Escobar|Pablo Escobar was killed on 2 December 1993 in Medellín, after a chase by the Colombian authorities. He was the head of the Medellín cartel.

bio|12-03|311|Διοκλητιανός|Diocletian|Diocletian was Roman emperor from 284 to 305. He established the Tetrarchy so that the empire could be governed more effectively, and he ordered the last great persecution of Christians. He resigned in 305 and died around 311, with no certainty about the month.
bio|12-03|1857|Τζόζεφ Κόνραντ|Joseph Conrad|Joseph Conrad was born in 1857 in present-day Ukraine, to Polish parents. He wrote in English and is known for "Heart of Darkness". He died in 1924.
bio|12-03|1894|Ρόμπερτ Λούις Στίβενσον|Robert Louis Stevenson|Robert Louis Stevenson died in 1894 in Samoa. He was a Scottish writer and wrote "Treasure Island".

bio|12-03|1919|Πιερ Ωγκύστ Ρενουάρ|Pierre-Auguste Renoir|Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French painter of Impressionism. He painted "Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette" as well as many portraits and scenes full of light. He died in 1919.
bio|12-03|1930|Ζαν-Λυκ Γκοντάρ|Jean-Luc Godard|Jean-Luc Godard was a French director and a leading figure of the "New Wave". He directed "Breathless". He died in 2022.
bio|12-03|1935|Σαρλ Ρισέ|Charles Richet|Charles Richet was a French physiologist. He discovered anaphylaxis and in 1913 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. He died in 1935.
bio|12-03|1948|Ozzy Osbourne|Ozzy Osbourne|Ozzy Osbourne was born in 1948 in Birmingham. He was the singer of Black Sabbath and an important figure of heavy metal. He died in 2025.
bio|12-03|1960|Τζούλιαν Μουρ|Julianne Moore|Julianne Moore is an American-British actress. She won an Oscar for "Still Alice" and appeared in "The Hours" and "Safe".
bio|12-03|1981|Νταβίντ Βίγια|David Villa|David Villa is a former Spanish footballer, a striker. He played for Valencia, Barcelona and Atlético Madrid and won the World Cup in 2010.

bio|12-04|1131|Ομάρ Καγιάμ|Omar Khayyam|Omar Khayyam was a Persian poet, astronomer and mathematician. He is known for the "Rubaiyat", quatrains translated into English by Edward FitzGerald. The date of his death is not certain.

bio|12-04|1679|Τόμας Χομπς|Thomas Hobbes|Thomas Hobbes was an English philosopher. In "Leviathan" he argued that people create the state through a social contract to avoid a war of all against all. He died in 1679.

bio|12-04|1795|Τόμας Κάρλαϊλ|Thomas Carlyle|Thomas Carlyle was a Scottish historian and philosopher. He wrote "The French Revolution" and "On Heroes, Hero-Worship and the Heroic in History". He died in 1881.

bio|12-04|1875|Ράινερ Μαρία Ρίλκε|Rainer Maria Rilke|Rainer Maria Rilke was born in Prague and wrote in German. He was a poet and wrote the "Duino Elegies" and "Letters to a Young Poet". He died in 1926.
bio|12-04|1892|Φρανθίσκο Φράνκο|Francisco Franco|Francisco Franco was born in 1892 in Ferrol. He was a general and ruled Spain as a dictator from 1939 to 1975.
bio|12-04|1949|Τζεφ Μπρίτζες|Jeff Bridges|Jeff Bridges is an American actor. He won an Oscar for "Crazy Heart" and appeared in "The Big Lebowski".
bio|12-04|1969|Jay-Z|Jay-Z|Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter, is an American rapper and businessman. He founded Roc-A-Fella Records and is married to Beyoncé.
bio|12-04|1975|Χάνα Άρεντ|Hannah Arendt|Hannah Arendt died in 1975 in New York. She was a German-Jewish political thinker and wrote "The Origins of Totalitarianism".

bio|12-04|1993|Φρανκ Ζάπα|Frank Zappa|Frank Zappa was an American musician. He was a guitarist and composer and the leader of the band The Mothers of Invention, with an experimental style. He died in 1993.

bio|12-05|1782|Μάρτιν Βαν Μπιούρεν|Martin Van Buren|Martin Van Buren was the 8th president of the United States, from 1837 to 1841. Before that he was vice president under Andrew Jackson. He died in 1862.

bio|12-05|1791|Βόλφγκανγκ Αμαντέους Μότσαρτ|Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart|Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart was an Austrian composer, one of the greatest in classical music. He wrote operas such as "The Marriage of Figaro" and "The Magic Flute". He died in Vienna in 1791, at the age of 35, leaving the Requiem unfinished.
bio|12-05|1803|Φιόντορ Τιούτσεφ|Fyodor Tyutchev|Fyodor Tyutchev was a Russian poet and diplomat. He wrote philosophical and lyrical poems about nature and love. He died in 1873.

bio|12-05|1867|Γιούζεφ Πιουσούτσκι|Józef Piłsudski|Józef Piłsudski was a Polish military officer and politician. He led the struggle for Polish independence in 1918 and became the strong man of the country. He died in 1935.

bio|12-05|1901|Βέρνερ Χάιζενμπεργκ|Werner Heisenberg|Werner Heisenberg was a German physicist and one of the founders of quantum mechanics. He formulated the uncertainty principle and in 1932 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1976.

bio|12-05|1901|Γουόλτ Ντίσνεϊ|Walt Disney|Walt Disney was an American producer and the creator of Mickey Mouse. He founded the Disney studios, produced the first full-length animated feature film, "Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs", and created Disneyland. He died in 1966.
bio|12-05|1925|Βλαντυσλάβ Ρέυμοντ|Władysław Reymont|Władysław Reymont was a Polish writer. He wrote the epic "The Peasants" and in 1924 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1925.
bio|12-05|1926|Κλωντ Μονέ|Claude Monet|Claude Monet died in 1926 at Giverny. He was a French painter and a leading figure of Impressionism, known for the "Water Lilies".

bio|12-05|1927|Πουμιπόν Αντουνιαντέτ|Bhumibol Adulyadej|Bhumibol Adulyadej, or Rama IX, was king of Thailand from 1946 to 2016. He was the longest-reigning monarch of the country and was very much loved.
bio|12-05|2013|Νέλσον Μαντέλα|Nelson Mandela|Nelson Mandela died on 5 December 2013, at the age of 95. He was the first black president of South Africa and a symbol of the struggle against apartheid.
bio|12-06|1185|Αλφόνσος Α΄|Afonso I|Afonso I was the first king of Portugal, from 1139. He won territory from the Moors and secured recognition of the independence of the state. He died in 1185.

bio|12-06|1421|Ερρίκος ΣΤ΄|Henry VI|Henry VI was king of England from 1422, as an infant, until 1461, and again from 1470. His reign was marked by the loss of France and the Wars of the Roses. He was killed in 1471.

bio|12-06|1478|Μπαλντασσάρε Καστιλιόνε|Baldassare Castiglione|Baldassare Castiglione was an Italian diplomat and writer. He wrote "The Book of the Courtier", a guide to the perfect courtier of the Renaissance. He died in 1529.

bio|12-06|1778|Ζοζέφ Λουί Γκαι-Λυσάκ|Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac|Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac was a French chemist and physicist. He formulated the laws of gases and studied the relationship between volume and temperature. He died in 1850.
bio|12-06|1882|Άντονι Τρόλοπ|Anthony Trollope|Anthony Trollope was an English writer. He wrote novels set in Barsetshire, among them "Barchester Towers", and the novels "Palliser". He died in 1882.
bio|12-06|1889|Τζέφερσον Ντέηβις|Jefferson Davis|Jefferson Davis was an American politician. He was president of the Confederate States of America during the Civil War. He died in 1889.

bio|12-06|1892|Βέρνερ φον Ζίμενς|Werner von Siemens|Werner von Siemens was a German inventor and businessman. He founded the company Siemens & Halske and developed the electric telegraph and the electric generator. He died in 1892.
bio|12-06|1979|Τιμ Κέιχιλ|Tim Cahill|Tim Cahill is a former Australian footballer, a midfielder. He played for Everton and was the first goalscorer for the Australian national team at the World Cups.
bio|12-07|983|Όθων Β΄|Otto II|Otto II was emperor of the Holy Roman Empire from 973. He married the Byzantine princess Theophanu and fought in Italy against the Saracens. He died in 983.

bio|12-07|1598|Τζιαν Λορέντσο Μπερνίνι|Gian Lorenzo Bernini|Gian Lorenzo Bernini was an Italian sculptor and architect of the Baroque. He created "The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa" and the square of Saint Peter's in Rome. He died in 1680.

bio|12-07|1894|Φερντινάν Λεσσέψ|Ferdinand de Lesseps|Ferdinand de Lesseps was a French diplomat and businessman. He led the construction of the Suez Canal, which opened in 1869, but the Panama Canal project failed. He died in 1894.

bio|12-07|1928|Νόαμ Τσόμσκι|Noam Chomsky|Noam Chomsky is an American linguist and philosopher. He developed generative grammar and is also known as a critic of the foreign policy of the United States.
bio|12-07|1932|Έλεν Μπέρστιν|Ellen Burstyn|Ellen Burstyn is an American actress. She won an Oscar for "Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore" and appeared in "The Exorcist".

bio|12-07|1956|Λάρι Μπερντ|Larry Bird|Larry Bird is a former American basketball player. He played for the Boston Celtics and won three NBA championships. He was one of the greatest players of his generation.
bio|12-07|1975|Θόρντον Ουάιλντερ|Thornton Wilder|Thornton Wilder was an American writer and playwright. He wrote the play "Our Town" and won three Pulitzer Prizes. He died in 1975.
bio|12-07|1980|Τζον Τέρι|John Terry|John Terry is a former English footballer, a defender. He played his entire career for Chelsea, as captain, and won the Champions League in 2012.
bio|12-07|1985|Ρόμπερτ Γκρέιβς|Robert Graves|Robert Graves died in 1985. He was an English poet and writer, known for "I, Claudius" and for his works on Greek myths.

bio|12-08|1542|Μαρία Α΄|Mary, Queen of Scots|Mary, Queen of Scots, was born in 1542 and became queen when only a few days old. She was forced to abdicate and was imprisoned in England by Elizabeth I. She was beheaded in 1587.

bio|12-08|1832|Μπιέρνστιερνε Μπιέρνσον|Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson|Bjørnstjerne Bjørnson was a Norwegian writer. He wrote poetry and plays and the national anthem of Norway. In 1903 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1910.
bio|12-08|1864|Τζορτζ Μπουλ|George Boole|George Boole died in 1864. He was an English mathematician, and the Boolean algebra he developed is the basis of digital computers.
bio|12-08|1865|Γιαν Σιμπέλιους|Jean Sibelius|Jean Sibelius was a Finnish composer. He wrote the symphonic poem "Finlandia" and seven symphonies. He died in 1957.

bio|12-08|1903|Χέρμπερτ Σπένσερ|Herbert Spencer|Herbert Spencer was an English philosopher and sociologist. He applied the ideas of evolution to society and coined the phrase "survival of the fittest". He died in 1903.
bio|12-08|1943|Τζιμ Μόρισον|Jim Morrison|Jim Morrison was the singer of the American band The Doors. He died in 1971 in Paris, at the age of 27.

bio|12-08|1978|Γκόλντα Μέιρ|Golda Meir|Golda Meir was an Israeli politician and the only woman to serve as prime minister of Israel, from 1969 to 1974. She was born in Kiev and grew up in the United States. She died in 1978.

bio|12-08|1980|Τζον Λένον|John Lennon|John Lennon was murdered on 8 December 1980 in New York, outside his home. He was the singer and co-founder of the Beatles, with a solo career and the song "Imagine".
bio|12-08|1982|Νίκι Μινάζ|Nicki Minaj|Nicki Minaj was born in Trinidad and grew up in New York. She is a rapper and singer who has released hits such as "Super Bass".
bio|12-09|1437|Σιγισμόνδος|Sigismund|Sigismund was Holy Roman Emperor from 1433 and king of Hungary and Bohemia. He convened the Council of Constance and fought the Ottomans. He died in 1437.
bio|12-09|1608|Τζον Μίλτον|John Milton|John Milton was an English poet. He wrote the epic "Paradise Lost" and supported freedom of the press. He died in 1674.
bio|12-09|1641|Άντονι βαν Ντάικ|Anthony van Dyck|Anthony van Dyck was a Flemish painter. He became court painter to Charles I of England and painted many portraits. He died in 1641.
bio|12-09|1842|Πιοτρ Κροπότκιν|Peter Kropotkin|Peter Kropotkin was a Russian anarchist and geographer. He wrote "Mutual Aid: A Factor of Evolution" and supported anarchist communism. He died in 1921.
bio|12-09|1916|Κερκ Ντάγκλας|Kirk Douglas|Kirk Douglas was an American actor. He starred in the films "Spartacus" and "Paths of Glory". He died in 2020, at the age of 103.
bio|12-09|1934|Τζούντι Ντεντς|Judi Dench|Judi Dench is an English actress. She won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for "Shakespeare in Love" and played "M" in the James Bond films.

bio|12-09|1937|Νιλς Γκούσταφ Νταλέν|Nils Gustaf Dalén|Nils Gustaf Dalén was a Swedish engineer. He invented automatic regulators for lighthouses and in 1912 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1937.

bio|12-09|1954|Ζαν-Κλοντ Γιούνκερ|Jean-Claude Juncker|Jean-Claude Juncker is a Luxembourgish politician. He was prime minister of Luxembourg and president of the European Commission from 2014 to 2019.
bio|12-09|1996|Μαίρη Λίκι|Mary Leakey|Mary Leakey was a British palaeoanthropologist. She discovered fossil hominid footprints at Laetoli in Tanzania, aged 3.6 million years. She died in 1996.

bio|12-10|1198|Αβερρόης|Averroes|Averroes, or Ibn Rushd, was an Andalusian philosopher, judge and physician. He wrote commentaries on Aristotle that influenced medieval thought. He died in 1198 in Marrakesh.

bio|12-10|1815|Άντα Λάβλεϊς|Ada Lovelace|Ada Lovelace was an English mathematician and the daughter of Lord Byron. She wrote the first program for Babbage's analytical engine and is regarded as the first female programmer. She died in 1852.

bio|12-10|1830|Έμιλι Ντίκινσον|Emily Dickinson|Emily Dickinson was an American poet. She lived in seclusion in Amherst and wrote more than 1,700 poems, most of which were published after her death. She died in 1886.

bio|12-10|1891|Νέλλυ Ζαχς|Nelly Sachs|Nelly Sachs was a German-Jewish poet. She left Germany for Sweden in 1940 and wrote poetry about the Holocaust. In 1966 she shared the Nobel Prize in Literature with Shmuel Agnon. She died in 1970.
bio|12-10|1896|Άλφρεντ Νόμπελ|Alfred Nobel|Alfred Nobel died in 1896 in San Remo. He was a Swedish chemist and industrialist, the inventor of dynamite, and in his will he founded the Nobel Prizes.

bio|12-10|1936|Λουίτζι Πιραντέλλο|Luigi Pirandello|Luigi Pirandello was an Italian writer and playwright. He wrote "Six Characters in Search of an Author" and in 1934 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1936.
bio|12-10|1957|Μάικλ Κλαρκ Ντάνκαν|Michael Clarke Duncan|Michael Clarke Duncan was an American actor. He was nominated for an Oscar for his role in "The Green Mile". He died in 2012.

bio|12-10|1987|Γκονσάλο Ιγουαΐν|Gonzalo Higuaín|Gonzalo Higuaín is a former Argentine footballer, a striker. He played for Real Madrid, Napoli and Juventus and took part in the final of the 2014 World Cup.
bio|12-10|2006|Αουγούστο Πινοσέτ|Augusto Pinochet|Augusto Pinochet died in 2006. He was a general and the dictator of Chile from 1973 to 1990, and he died without having been convicted.
bio|12-11|1803|Εκτόρ Μπερλιόζ|Hector Berlioz|Hector Berlioz was a French composer of Romanticism. He wrote the "Symphonie fantastique" and the opera "The Trojans". He died in 1869.

bio|12-11|1843|Ρόμπερτ Κοχ|Robert Koch|Robert Koch was a German physician and microbiologist. He discovered the bacteria that cause tuberculosis and cholera, and in 1905 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. He died in 1910.

bio|12-11|1882|Μαξ Μπορν|Max Born|Max Born was a German physicist. He contributed to quantum mechanics and in 1954 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He left Germany under the Nazi regime. He died in 1970.
